summary: Enterprise Suite AC-05 incident rollback/quarantine metadata foundation for unhealthy runtime events.

findings: The domain function performs one narrow validation pass for incident rollback planning: tenant/incident identity, rollback-or-quarantine-first sequencing, manual SSH refusal, audit evidence refs, OpenTofu/ops convergence, and idempotency.
The app function only projects an already-validated plan into a metadata envelope, with no hidden runtime execution or side effects.
Rollback/quarantine-first policy and OpenTofu/ops convergence refs mirror hyperscaler incident discipline without claiming a deployed control plane.
Manual SSH refusal preserves the ADR-0349 no-manual-deploy posture and keeps later incident adapters on auditable substrate boundaries.

F3_adversarial.failing_fixture_id: manual SSH route refusal, remediation-before-rollback refusal, missing incident evidence refusal, and missing OpenTofu/ops convergence refusal
F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Tests fail if incident response uses manual SSH, remediates before rollback/quarantine, omits incident JSON/evidence, or bypasses OpenTofu/ops convergence refs.
findings: AC-05 now has direct positive and negative test coverage in the flat microservice crate path.
The app envelope test confirms the validated metadata remains a non-executing incident rollback handoff.
Types mirror the acceptance wording: IncidentTrigger, IncidentFirstAction, IncidentRemediationRoute, IncidentRollbackInput, and IncidentRollbackPlan.
The test names and spec test_ref now point to implemented AC-05 incident tests.
cargo fmt, locked suite tests, locked suite clippy, and 11-package enterprise regression checks passed locally.
No dependency, catalog, lockfile, runtime adapter, storage adapter, or deployment artifact was added in this slice.

alternatives_named: reuse the generic ops command envelope only
implement a runtime rollback executor now
model AC-05 as pure domain/app metadata now
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: A dedicated pure metadata plan/envelope satisfies AC-05 invariants while avoiding premature runtime rollback, incident emitter, or cloud adapter claims.
rejected_reasons: A generic ops command alone would not encode rollback/quarantine-first sequencing or mandatory incident evidence.
A runtime executor would exceed the current domain/app foundation slice and require storage, deploy, and SLO evidence not present in this branch.

findings: The plan requires tenant id, incident id, canary/incident/rollback audit evidence refs, convergence ref, and idempotency key.
Manual SSH is modeled as an explicit refused remediation route rather than omitted from the type system.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: No deployed runtime path exists; validation performs bounded string prefix checks and no I/O.

findings.summary: Incident rollback planning is O(1) with fixed field validation and does not allocate beyond the returned metadata plan.

findings: Public fields carry data_class annotations and output metadata is wrapped in Classified values.
The slice records evidence refs and metadata envelopes only; it does not claim durable incident emission, SLO measurement, compliance certification, or runtime rollback execution.
The change is additive inside existing suite crates and can be reverted without data migration, durable state rewrite, or external resource teardown.
The app envelope carries a stable incident rollback topic plus canary, incident, rollback, and convergence refs for later adapters.
Audit-chain JSONL rows record local evidence attachment and local Oya VCS closeout; no runtime log, metric, trace, or incident event emission is claimed.
Enterprise Suite AC-05 test_ref moved from a stale root-crate path to implemented flat microservice domain/app test paths.

M1_challenge_assumption.premise_stated: An incident rollback foundation can be useful before runtime integration only if it encodes deterministic safety invariants and remains metadata-only.
M1_challenge_assumption.premise_evidence_ref: specs/microservices/enterprise-suite.json AC-05 and ADR-0349 no-manual-deploy posture
M1_challenge_assumption.do_nothing_consequence: AC-05 would remain a spec statement while later runtime work could accidentally add manual SSH remediation or remediation-before-rollback behavior.
M1_challenge_assumption.upstream_fix_rejection_reason: Waiting for full incident runtime would mix pure safety invariants with storage, deploy, SLO, and adapter concerns.

findings: This slice deepens ERP composition by adding suite-wide incident response metadata that protects HR, Payroll, and Accounting runtime composition without direct child-service coupling.
Names use Enterprise Suite, incident, rollback, quarantine, OpenTofu, and ops vocabulary already present in the acceptance criterion and deployment contract.
Plan, todo, and spec AC-05 now document the incident rollback foundation and its non-claims.
Domain validation remains in the suite domain crate and metadata-envelope preparation remains in the suite app crate.
No runtime rollback executor, incident emitter, storage repository, HTTP router, Workflow client, ArgoCD Application, Helm chart, or cloud deployment artifact was introduced.
The slice adds no third-party dependencies and no workspace dependency changes.
AC-05 now has concrete test refs and typed metadata structures with schema_version fields.
Required incident checks are deterministic prefix and enum checks over explicit fields.
